experience.guidance: Focus on architecture, scale, and performance improvements. Use strict formatting: 'Action + Methodology/Tech + Result (Latency reduced by X ms, handled Y TPS)'.
common_mistakes: Writing 'Worked on backend' instead of 'Architected REST APIs using Node.js'

projects.guidance: Highlight complex, deployed systems. Open-source contributions (GSoC) and major BTPs are highly valued. Include GitHub links if possible.
common_mistakes: Listing simple CRUD apps with no users or scale

por.guidance: Focus on Tech Team leads (e.g., Web & Coding Club Manager, Techfest Coordinator).

scholastic.guidance: Highlight Competitive Programming ranks (Codeforces, ICPC), Hackathon wins, and core CS coursework.
common_mistakes: Not mentioning LeetCode/Codeforces handles if they are strong

extracurricular.guidance: Keep minimal. Use space for more technical projects.

leadership_stakeholder_mgmt.description: Demonstrated ability to lead teams, manage stakeholders, and drive organizational change.

strategic_problem_solving.description: Evidence of structured, analytical thinking applied to real-world problems.

financial_quantitative_rigor.description: Presence of hard metrics, financial figures, and data-driven outcomes.

product_technical_execution.description: Technical skills used as a means to business ends, or core technical delivery.

entrepreneurial_ownership.description: Self-started initiatives, side projects, or entrepreneurial ventures.

phrasing_rules: Every bullet must pass the 'So What?' test — state the result, not just the action.
Lead with non-repetitive power verbs: Spearheaded, Orchestrated, Synthesized, Catalyzed.
Include at least one quantified metric per experience/POR point.
Use the Action + Context + Impact structure consistently.
Keep each bullet to exactly 1 line on a standard template.
Do not use full stops at the end of bullet points.
Avoid explaining too much in a single point; focus on the outcome.
